introduction: This spec completes the audit subsystem by adding agent session lifecycle tracking (open/close/usage APIs), a Prometheus-compatible `/metrics` scrape endpoint, and a background retention worker that enforces time-based and run-count limits on the DuckDB audit database. Note: requirements referencing `github.com/prometheus/client_golang` APIs are based on PRD descriptions and should be cross-checked against the installed library version before implementation.

glossary.AF_AUDIT_MAX_AGE_DAYS: Environment variable controlling the maximum age in days for retained audit event records (default 90).
glossary.AF_AUDIT_MAX_RUNS: Environment variable controlling the maximum number of distinct run_ids to retain (default 50).
glossary.AF_AUDIT_ORPHAN_RETENTION_DAYS: Environment variable controlling the grace period in days before orphaned audit data (workspace no longer in SQLite) is deleted (default 30).
glossary.AF_POSTMORTEM_MAX_AGE_DAYS: Environment variable controlling the maximum age in days for retained postmortem records (default 180).
glossary.AF_SESSION_MAX_ACTIVE_AGE_DAYS: Environment variable controlling the maximum age in days for active (orphaned) sessions before the retention worker force-closes them with status 'timeout' (default 7).
glossary.AF_SESSION_MAX_AGE_DAYS: Environment variable controlling the maximum age in days for retained completed session records (default 90).
glossary.AF_TRACE_MAX_AGE_DAYS: Environment variable controlling the maximum age in days for retained trace records (default 30).
glossary.Emitter: The audit.Emitter interface defined in spec 17 (internal/audit/emitter.go). Spec 19 receives an audit.Emitter dependency injected at startup — it does not create its own.
glossary.HubEvent: Go struct defined in spec 17 representing a hub-internal audit event, with fields EventType, ActorType, ActorID, ResourceType, ResourceID, Action, Workspace, and Metadata.
glossary.StartRetentionWorker: Go function in the audit package that starts the background retention worker goroutine.
glossary.Store: Go interface defined in spec 17 providing DuckDB-backed persistence for all audit tables.
glossary.active: Session status indicating the session is open and accepting usage reports.
glossary.admin_token: Credential type string value indicating the caller is an administrator with implicit full access to all scopes and workspaces.
glossary.afhub_agent_sessions_active: Prometheus gauge metric tracking currently active sessions, labeled by workspace.
glossary.afhub_agent_tokens_total: Prometheus counter metric tracking token usage, labeled by workspace, model, and direction.
glossary.afhub_audit_events_total: Prometheus counter metric tracking total audit events ingested, labeled by source and event_type.
glossary.afhub_audit_table_rows: Prometheus gauge metric tracking row count per audit table, sampled hourly by the retention worker.
glossary.afhub_http_request_duration_seconds: Prometheus histogram metric tracking HTTP request latency in seconds, labeled by method and path.
glossary.afhub_http_requests_total: Prometheus counter metric tracking total HTTP requests, labeled by method, path, and status.
glossary.afhub_jobqueue_depth: Prometheus gauge metric tracking job queue depth, labeled by type and status; defined here but owned and initialized by the durable_job_queue subsystem.
glossary.afhub_retention_errors_total: Prometheus counter metric tracking retention step failures, labeled by step name.
glossary.afhub_retention_last_run_timestamp_secon: Prometheus gauge metric recording the Unix timestamp of the last fully successful retention worker run.
glossary.afhub_sse_connections: Prometheus gauge metric tracking active SSE connections.
glossary.agent_audit_events: DuckDB table (defined in spec 17) storing structured audit events emitted by agents.
glossary.agent_sessions: DuckDB table (defined in spec 17) that stores the lifecycle record of each agent session, including status, credential info, and timing.
glossary.agent_traces: DuckDB table (defined in spec 17) storing distributed trace data from agents.
glossary.api_key: Credential type string value for workspace-scoped API keys.
glossary.apikit: Internal framework providing authentication middleware, permission enforcement, and standard error-response helpers used across all hub handlers.
glossary.apikit.AuthInfo: Struct from apikit carrying the authenticated caller's credential_id and credential_type for the current request.
glossary.apikit.WriteAPIError: Helper function from apikit that writes a standard hub error envelope {error: string, status: int} to the HTTP response.
glossary.archetype: Agent archetype label associated with a session.
glossary.audit:read: Permission scope (defined in spec 17 in internal/audit/permissions.go) required to query audit events.
glossary.audit:write: Permission scope (defined in spec 17 in internal/audit/permissions.go) required to ingest audit events.
glossary.c.Path(): Echo framework method returning the matched route template string (e.g. /api/v1/sessions/:id) rather than the raw request URI, used as the path label in Prometheus HTTP metrics.
glossary.cache_creation_input_tokens: Session-level summary field on the complete endpoint representing tokens consumed creating cache entries across all API calls in the session.
glossary.cache_read_input_tokens: Tokens read from cache during a session, reported on the complete endpoint.
glossary.cache_read_tokens: Tokens read from cache during a single incremental usage report.
glossary.completed: Terminal session status indicating the session ended successfully.
glossary.credential_id: Unique identifier of the credential (API key, PAT, or admin token) that opened or is acting on a session.
glossary.credential_type: String discriminator for the credential kind: admin_token, api_key, or pat.
glossary.failed: Terminal session status indicating the session ended with an error.
glossary.force-close: System-initiated operation that sets all active sessions for a workspace to terminated status during workspace archive or delete.
glossary.group_by: Query parameter on the cost endpoint controlling the breakdown dimension: day, session, or model.
glossary.hub.session.force_closed: Audit event type emitted when a session is force-closed due to workspace archive or delete.
glossary.hub_audit_events: DuckDB table (defined in spec 17) storing structured audit events emitted by the hub itself.
glossary.internal/audit/handlers.go: Existing Go source file extended with session, usage, cost, and single-session-fetch HTTP handlers.
glossary.internal/audit/metrics.go: New Go source file containing the custom Prometheus registry, metric definitions, and Echo middleware factory.
glossary.internal/audit/retention.go: New Go source file containing the background retention worker implementation.
glossary.internal/audit/routes.go: Existing Go source file extended to register session, usage, cost, and metrics routes.
glossary.internal/audit/store.go: Existing Go source file extended with session CRUD, token usage, cost aggregation, and retention query methods.
glossary.internal/workspace/handlers.go: Existing Go source file modified to call session force-close in archive and delete handlers.
glossary.keyset cursor: Opaque pagination token encoding a (field, id) tuple, URL-safe base64-encoded per RFC 4648 §5 without padding, used for stable keyset-based pagination.
glossary.max_age_days: Retention configuration value controlling the maximum age of audit event records.
glossary.max_runs: Retention configuration value controlling the maximum number of distinct run_ids to retain.
glossary.node_id: Task graph node identifier associated with a session.
glossary.orphan_retention_days: Grace period after workspace deletion before orphaned audit data is purged by the retention worker.
glossary.pat: Credential type string value for Personal Access Tokens, which require explicit scope grants at issuance time.
glossary.postmortem_max_age_days: Retention configuration value controlling the maximum age of postmortem records.
glossary.postmortems: DuckDB table (defined in spec 17) storing post-mortem analysis records.
glossary.promhttp: Package from github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/promhttp providing the HTTP handler for Prometheus scrape endpoints.
glossary.retention worker: Background goroutine started at hub startup that runs immediately and then every hour to enforce retention policies on all audit tables.
glossary.run_id: Identifier grouping multiple audit events and sessions that belong to the same agent run.
glossary.session_max_age_days: Retention configuration value controlling the maximum age of completed session records.
glossary.sessions:read: Permission scope (defined in spec 17 in internal/audit/permissions.go) required to read session records, usage records, and cost summaries.
glossary.sessions:write: Permission scope (defined in spec 17 in internal/audit/permissions.go) required to open, close, or report usage on agent sessions.
glossary.terminated: Internal-only session status set exclusively by force-close logic when a workspace is archived or deleted.
glossary.timeout: Terminal session status indicating the session ended due to a timeout.
glossary.token_summary: Aggregated token usage counts (input, output, cache_read) and distinct models list computed at query time from token_usage rows for a session.
glossary.token_usage: DuckDB table (defined in spec 17) that stores incremental token consumption records linked to a session.
glossary.trace_max_age_days: Retention configuration value controlling the maximum age of trace records.
glossary.workspace_slug: URL-safe string identifier for a workspace, used as the primary workspace reference across all hub APIs.

user_story.goal: open a new session via POST /api/v1/sessions with workspace and optional metadata
user_story.benefit: so that the hub can track the session lifecycle and associate token usage with the correct workspace

acceptance_criteria.action: create a new agent_sessions record with status active, extract credential_id and credential_type from apikit.AuthInfo, generate a UUID if id is not provided, and return the session
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 201 with JSON body {id: string, workspace_slug: string, credential_id: string, credential_type: string, status: 'active', started_at: RFC3339 timestamp}
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller with sessions:write permission sends POST /api/v1/sessions with a valid workspace_slug

acceptance_criteria.action: return the existing session record without creating a duplicate
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the existing session JSON body in the same shape as the 201 response
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions with an id that already exists in agent_sessions

acceptance_criteria.action: reject the request using apikit.WriteAPIError with status 400 and message 'workspace_slug is required'
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with JSON body {error: 'workspace_slug is required', status: 400}
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: workspace_slug is missing or empty in the POST /api/v1/sessions request body

acceptance_criteria.action: reject the request with 403 Forbidden; for PAT credentials, the handler must verify that auth.Permissions contains workspace_slug+':agent:write' (or an equivalent workspace-scoped write permission) before creating the session; admin_token credentials bypass this check
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 when the PAT caller does not hold the required workspace-scoped permission for the target workspace_slug
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the caller's credential_type is 'pat' and auth.Permissions does not contain the workspace-scoped agent:write permission for the requested workspace_slug

edge_cases.action: reject the request via apikit auth middleware
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403
edge_cases.error_condition: the caller does not have sessions:write permission when sending POST /api/v1/sessions

edge_cases.action: create the session with run_id, node_id, archetype, model set to empty string and metadata set to null
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 201 with a valid session record
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions with all optional fields omitted

edge_cases.action: return an internal server error
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 500
edge_cases.error_condition: the DuckDB insert fails while processing a POST /api/v1/sessions request with a valid workspace_slug

edge_cases.action: one request creates the record and the other returns the existing record idempotently; no duplicate rows are created in agent_sessions
edge_cases.return_contract: both requests return HTTP 200 or 201 with the same session record
edge_cases.trigger: two concurrent callers send POST /api/v1/sessions with the same id simultaneously

user_story.goal: close an active session via POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete with final status and token usage
user_story.benefit: so that the hub records the terminal state and usage summary for the session

acceptance_criteria.action: set the session status to the provided terminal status (completed, failed, or timeout), record ended_at, duration_ms, error_message, and cache_creation_input_tokens, decrement afhub_agent_sessions_active gauge for the session's workspace, and return the updated session record
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the updated session JSON body including the actual status field
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the session owner or an admin_token caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete on an active session

acceptance_criteria.action: return the existing session record without modification
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the existing session JSON body including the actual status field
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete on a session already in any terminal state (completed, failed, timeout, or terminated)

acceptance_criteria.action: reject the request with 403 Forbidden
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 403
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the caller's credential_id does not match the session's credential_id and the caller's credential_type is not admin_token when sending POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete

acceptance_criteria.action: return 404 Not Found
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: no session with the given id exists in agent_sessions when a caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete

acceptance_criteria.action: use a conditional DuckDB UPDATE: UPDATE agent_sessions SET status=?, ended_at=? WHERE session_id=? AND status='active'; if 0 rows are affected, return a sentinel error ErrSessionNotActive and the handler returns 409 Conflict to the caller
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: the UPDATE is atomic and conditional; concurrent PATCH requests for the same session cannot both decrement the afhub_agent_sessions_active gauge — only the request that successfully transitions the session from active wins; the second request receives 409 Conflict
acceptance_criteria.note: This prevents the double-decrement bug where two concurrent requests both observe status='active' and both decrement the gauge

edge_cases.action: reject the request with 400 Bad Request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete with status set to 'terminated', which is not a valid client-settable terminal status

edge_cases.action: allow the operation and close the session
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the updated session record
edge_cases.trigger: an admin_token caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete on a session owned by a different credential_id

edge_cases.action: return the existing terminated session record without modification, treating all terminal states uniformly
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the session record showing status: 'terminated'
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete on a terminated session

edge_cases.action: return an internal server error without modifying the afhub_agent_sessions_active gauge
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 500
edge_cases.error_condition: the DuckDB update fails while processing a POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete request

user_story.goal: report incremental token usage via POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage during an active session
user_story.benefit: so that the hub accumulates accurate per-call token consumption for cost tracking

acceptance_criteria.action: create a new token_usage record linked to the session, resolving workspace_slug from the session record, and return the created record
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 201 with JSON body {id: string, session_id: string, workspace_slug: string, model: string, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int, cache_read_tokens: int, reported_at: RFC3339 timestamp}
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the session owner or an admin_token caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage with a valid model on an active session

acceptance_criteria.action: return 404 Not Found
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: no session with the given id exists in agent_sessions when a caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage

acceptance_criteria.action: reject the request with 403 Forbidden
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 403
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the caller's credential_id does not match the session's credential_id and the caller's credential_type is not admin_token when sending POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage

acceptance_criteria.action: reject the request with 409 Conflict
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 409 with JSON body {error: 'session is not active'}
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: a caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage on a session whose status is completed, failed, timeout, or terminated

acceptance_criteria.action: reject the request with 400 Bad Request
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the model field is missing or empty in the POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage request body

acceptance_criteria.action: reject the request with 422 Unprocessable Entity using apikit.WriteAPIError with message 'token counts must be non-negative'; this validation MUST occur before any DuckDB write
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 422 with JSON body {error: 'token counts must be non-negative'}
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: any of input_tokens, output_tokens, or cache_read_tokens in the POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage request body is a negative integer

edge_cases.action: create a separate token_usage record for each call, each with its own generated id and reported_at timestamp
edge_cases.return_contract: each call returns HTTP 201 with a distinct token_usage record
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage multiple times on the same active session

edge_cases.action: return the existing token_usage record without creating a duplicate (idempotent by id)
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 201 with the existing token_usage record
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage with a duplicate id field

edge_cases.action: return an internal server error
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 500
edge_cases.error_condition: the DuckDB insert fails while processing a POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage request on an active session

edge_cases.action: allow the operation and create the token_usage record
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 201 with the created token_usage record
edge_cases.trigger: an admin_token caller sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage on a session owned by a different credential_id

user_story.goal: list agent sessions with filtering and cursor pagination via GET /api/v1/sessions
user_story.benefit: so that I can monitor and audit session activity across workspaces

acceptance_criteria.action: return a paginated list of sessions visible to the caller, with token_summary aggregated from token_usage rows for each session, applying any provided filters (workspace_slug, run_id, status, credential_type, since, order, limit, cursor). When a workspace_slug filter is provided, the DuckDB query MUST include WHERE workspace_slug = :workspace_slug to guarantee isolation between workspaces.
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with JSON body {sessions: [...], next_cursor: string|null, has_more: bool}
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller with sessions:read permission sends GET /api/v1/sessions

acceptance_criteria.action: restrict results to sessions in workspaces the caller has access to; when workspace_slug filter is provided for an inaccessible workspace, return 403; when no workspace_slug filter is provided, silently exclude inaccessible workspaces
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 when explicit workspace_slug filter targets an inaccessible workspace; otherwise returns HTTP 200 with filtered results
acceptance_criteria.state: the caller's credential_type is not admin_token

acceptance_criteria.action: apply keyset pagination using the decoded (started_at, id) tuple from the cursor, filtering with < for desc order and > for asc order, and include next_cursor in the response if more records exist
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the correct page of sessions and a valid next_cursor or null
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions with a cursor parameter

acceptance_criteria.action: return sessions across all workspaces without access restriction
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with sessions from all workspaces

edge_cases.action: cap the limit at 500
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with at most 500 sessions
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions with limit exceeding 500

edge_cases.action: use the default page size of 50
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with at most 50 sessions
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions with no limit parameter

edge_cases.action: return 400 Bad Request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions with a malformed or tampered cursor that cannot be decoded or parsed as a valid (started_at, id) tuple

edge_cases.action: return only sessions with terminated status, since terminated is a valid filter value
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with sessions filtered to terminated status
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions with status filter set to 'terminated'

edge_cases.action: keyset cursor pagination ensures no records are skipped or duplicated across pages
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with consistent page results
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions and new sessions are inserted concurrently during pagination

user_story.goal: fetch a single session record by ID via GET /api/v1/sessions/:id
user_story.benefit: so that I can inspect the full details and token summary of a specific session

acceptance_criteria.action: return the session record with token_summary aggregated from all token_usage rows for that session. The DuckDB query MUST scope results to the caller's accessible workspaces; a session_id belonging to a workspace the caller cannot access returns 404 (not the session record).
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the full session JSON object including token_summary
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller with sessions:read permission sends GET /api/v1/sessions/:id for a session in an accessible workspace

acceptance_criteria.action: return 404 Not Found
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: no session with the given id exists in agent_sessions when a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions/:id

acceptance_criteria.action: return 403 Forbidden
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 403
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: a non-admin caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions/:id for a session that exists but whose workspace the caller cannot access

edge_cases.action: return the session record regardless of workspace access
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the full session JSON object
edge_cases.trigger: an admin_token caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions/:id for a session in any workspace

edge_cases.action: return the session with token_summary showing all zero counts and an empty models_used list
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with token_summary {total_input_tokens: 0, total_output_tokens: 0, total_cache_read_tokens: 0, models_used: []}
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions/:id for a session with no token_usage records

user_story.goal: query paginated token usage records for a session via GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage
user_story.benefit: so that I can audit per-call token consumption and verify session totals

acceptance_criteria.action: return a paginated page of token_usage records for the session and the unbounded totals aggregated across all token_usage records ever recorded for the session. The handler first loads the session record; if the session's workspace_slug is not accessible to the caller, return 404. This ensures a session_id belonging to a different workspace cannot be probed via this endpoint.
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with JSON body {session_id: string, records: [...], totals: {total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, total_cache_read_tokens, models_used}, next_cursor: string|null, has_more: bool}
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller with sessions:read permission sends GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage for an accessible session

acceptance_criteria.action: return 404 Not Found
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: no session with the given id exists when a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage

acceptance_criteria.action: return 403 Forbidden
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 403
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: a non-admin caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage for a session that exists but whose workspace the caller cannot access

acceptance_criteria.action: compute the totals field by aggregating all token_usage records ever recorded for the session, independent of pagination page or any time range filter
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: totals values are consistent across all pages and reflect the complete session history

edge_cases.action: cap the limit at 1000
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with at most 1000 records
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage with limit exceeding 1000

edge_cases.action: use the default page size of 100
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with at most 100 records
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage with no limit parameter

edge_cases.action: return 400 Bad Request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller sends GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage with a malformed cursor that cannot be decoded as a valid (reported_at, id) tuple

edge_cases.action: keyset cursor pagination ensures no records are skipped or duplicated across pages
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with consistent page results
edge_cases.trigger: a caller pages through GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage while new usage records are inserted concurrently

user_story.goal: retrieve aggregated token usage for a workspace over a time period via GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost
user_story.benefit: so that I can monitor token consumption and identify cost trends by day, session, or model

acceptance_criteria.action: aggregate token_usage records within the [since, until) time window (filtered by reported_at), group by the group_by dimension, and return totals and breakdown; the sessions count reflects distinct session IDs with at least one token_usage record in the period
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with JSON body {workspace: string, period: {since, until}, totals: {input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, sessions}, breakdown: [{<discriminator>: string, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, sessions}]}
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller with sessions:read permission sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost for an accessible workspace

acceptance_criteria.action: return 400 Bad Request with a descriptive error message
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with JSON body {error: 'since must be before until'}
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: a caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost with since greater than or equal to until

acceptance_criteria.action: return 403 Forbidden
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 403
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: a non-admin caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost for a workspace slug they cannot access

acceptance_criteria.action: default since to 24 hours ago and until to now
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with results for the last 24 hours
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost with no since or until parameters

edge_cases.action: return breakdown entries with a date discriminator field (e.g. '2026-09-01') for each day in the period
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with breakdown entries each containing a 'date' field
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost with group_by=day

edge_cases.action: return breakdown entries with a session_id discriminator field for each distinct session
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with breakdown entries each containing a 'session_id' field
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost with group_by=session

edge_cases.action: return breakdown entries with a model discriminator field for each distinct model
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with breakdown entries each containing a 'model' field
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost with group_by=model

edge_cases.action: return zero totals and an empty breakdown array
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with totals all zero and breakdown: []
edge_cases.trigger: a caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost for a workspace with no token_usage records in the period

edge_cases.action: return cost data regardless of workspace access
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the cost summary
edge_cases.trigger: an admin_token caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost for any workspace

edge_cases.action: return 400 Bad Request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost with a group_by value that is not one of day, session, or model

user_story.goal: force-close all active sessions when a workspace is archived
user_story.benefit: so that agents cannot continue reporting usage on a workspace that is no longer active

acceptance_criteria.action: force-close all active sessions for the workspace by setting status to terminated, ended_at to the archive timestamp, and error_message to 'workspace archived'; decrement afhub_agent_sessions_active for each closed session; emit a hub.session.force_closed HubEvent via Emitter for each session with ActorType='system', ActorID='', ResourceType='session', Action='terminate', and Metadata containing session_id and reason='workspace archived'
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: all active sessions for the workspace are persisted with terminated status before the archive response is returned
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the workspace archive handler successfully updates the workspace status

acceptance_criteria.action: leave sessions in non-active states (completed, failed, timeout, terminated) unmodified during force-close
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: only active sessions are updated; all other sessions retain their existing status

edge_cases.action: log a warning via slog and proceed with the archive operation; do not abort the archive
edge_cases.return_contract: the workspace archive response is returned; sessions may remain in active state and will be cleaned up by the retention worker
edge_cases.error_condition: the DuckDB force-close operation fails when the workspace archive handler attempts to force-close sessions

edge_cases.action: complete without error and without emitting any HubEvents
edge_cases.return_contract: the archive response is returned normally
edge_cases.trigger: the workspace archive handler runs force-close on a workspace with no active sessions

edge_cases.action: log the error via slog and continue emitting events for remaining sessions
edge_cases.return_contract: the archive operation completes; emission failures are logged but do not abort the force-close
edge_cases.error_condition: the Emitter returns an error when attempting to emit a hub.session.force_closed event for one session during workspace archive

user_story.goal: force-close all active sessions before a workspace is deleted
user_story.benefit: so that session records are cleanly terminated before cascade deletes and audit data is preserved for the retention grace period

acceptance_criteria.action: force-close all active sessions for the workspace by setting status to terminated, ended_at to the deletion timestamp, and error_message to 'workspace deleted'; decrement afhub_agent_sessions_active for each closed session; emit a hub.session.force_closed HubEvent via Emitter for each session with reason='workspace deleted'
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: all active sessions are persisted with terminated status before the workspace row is deleted
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the workspace delete handler is invoked before the workspace row is deleted from SQLite

acceptance_criteria.action: retain audit data (agent_sessions, token_usage, hub_audit_events, agent_audit_events) after workspace deletion; orphaned audit data is cleaned up by the retention worker after orphan_retention_days
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: audit tables are not cascade-deleted when the workspace row is removed from SQLite

edge_cases.action: log a warning via slog and proceed with the SQLite workspace deletion; sessions may remain active and will be treated as orphans by the retention worker
edge_cases.return_contract: the workspace delete response is returned; the DuckDB failure is logged
edge_cases.error_condition: the DuckDB force-close operation fails when the workspace delete handler attempts to force-close sessions

edge_cases.action: return the SQLite error to the caller; sessions remain safely closed in DuckDB
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 500; sessions are terminated in DuckDB regardless
edge_cases.error_condition: the SQLite workspace deletion fails after DuckDB sessions have already been force-closed

user_story.benefit: so that I can monitor hub health, request rates, session activity, and queue depth via Prometheus

acceptance_criteria.action: return all registered metrics in Prometheus text exposition format using promhttp from the custom registry
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/plain; version=0.0.4 and Prometheus-formatted metric lines
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a Prometheus scraper sends GET /metrics

acceptance_criteria.action: expose the endpoint without authentication on the public port, mounted outside the API auth middleware group following the same pattern as internal/gitserver
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: GET /metrics returns HTTP 200 without requiring any Authorization header

acceptance_criteria.action: use c.Path() as the path label value in afhub_http_requests_total and afhub_http_request_duration_seconds to prevent cardinality explosion from unique path parameter values
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: path labels contain route templates such as /api/v1/sessions/:id rather than resolved URIs

acceptance_criteria.action: use a custom Prometheus registry (not the global default) for all afhub_* metrics to avoid conflicts with other registered metrics
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: the custom registry is passed to promhttp handler; global default registry metrics are not included in /metrics output

edge_cases.action: increment afhub_http_requests_total with method, path (from c.Path()), and status labels; observe afhub_http_request_duration_seconds with method and path labels
edge_cases.return_contract: metric values are updated before the next scrape
edge_cases.trigger: an HTTP request is made to any registered Echo route

edge_cases.action: register all afhub_* metrics with the custom registry; afhub_jobqueue_depth label combinations are initialized by the durable_job_queue subsystem and may be absent until that subsystem starts
edge_cases.return_contract: all metrics except afhub_jobqueue_depth appear in /metrics output immediately after startup
edge_cases.trigger: the hub starts up

edge_cases.action: use the standard latency buckets: 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0 seconds
edge_cases.return_contract: the histogram exposes exactly these bucket boundaries in /metrics output
edge_cases.trigger: the histogram is registered

user_story.goal: observe accurate metric values for sessions, tokens, SSE connections, and audit events
user_story.benefit: so that I can alert on anomalies and track system health in real time

acceptance_criteria.action: decrement afhub_agent_sessions_active gauge for the session's workspace_slug label
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: the gauge value for the workspace decreases by 1 immediately after the status transition
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a session transitions from active to any terminal status (completed, failed, timeout, or terminated)

acceptance_criteria.action: increment afhub_agent_sessions_active gauge for the session's workspace_slug label
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: the gauge value for the workspace increases by 1 after the session is persisted
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a new session is created via POST /api/v1/sessions

acceptance_criteria.action: increment afhub_agent_tokens_total counter with workspace, model, and direction labels (input, output, cache_read) for each non-zero token count
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: counter values increase by the reported token amounts
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a token_usage record is created via POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage

acceptance_criteria.action: increment afhub_audit_events_total counter with source and event_type labels
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: counter value increases by 1 per ingested event
acceptance_criteria.trigger: an audit event is ingested

edge_cases.action: do not increment afhub_agent_sessions_active again for the duplicate call
edge_cases.return_contract: gauge value is unchanged after the duplicate open
edge_cases.trigger: POST /api/v1/sessions is called with a duplicate id (idempotent open)

edge_cases.action: do not decrement afhub_agent_sessions_active again for the idempotent close
edge_cases.return_contract: gauge value is unchanged after the idempotent close
edge_cases.trigger: POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete is called on an already-terminal session (idempotent close)

user_story.goal: have the retention worker start immediately on hub startup and run every hour thereafter
user_story.benefit: so that stale data from a previous hub instance is cleaned up promptly without waiting up to one hour

acceptance_criteria.action: execute an immediate retention run before the first ticker fires, then repeat every hour using a time.Ticker, selecting on ctx.Done() between ticks
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: the goroutine runs the first retention pass synchronously before returning to the tick loop; subsequent runs occur at hourly intervals
acceptance_criteria.trigger: StartRetentionWorker is called from main.go with a context, Store, and SQLite DB reference

acceptance_criteria.action: exit the goroutine cleanly; if a retention run is in progress, complete the current step's DuckDB operation and skip remaining steps
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: the goroutine exits without starting new steps after cancellation; at most one extra step completes after shutdown is requested
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the context passed to StartRetentionWorker is cancelled (e.g. on SIGTERM)

edge_cases.action: check ctx.Err() before each step and exit immediately if the context is already cancelled
edge_cases.return_contract: no further steps are executed after cancellation is detected
edge_cases.trigger: the context is cancelled while the retention worker is between steps

edge_cases.action: the immediate startup run cleans up stale data from the previous instance without requiring a full hour wait
edge_cases.return_contract: stale data is pruned within seconds of hub startup
edge_cases.trigger: the hub restarts after a crash

user_story.goal: have the retention worker enforce all configured retention policies on each hourly run
user_story.benefit: so that the DuckDB audit database does not grow unboundedly

acceptance_criteria.action: delete records from all agent tables older than AF_AUDIT_MAX_AGE_DAYS
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: rows older than the configured max age are removed; newer rows are retained
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a retention run executes step 1

acceptance_criteria.action: if the count of distinct run_ids in agent_audit_events exceeds AF_AUDIT_MAX_RUNS, delete the oldest runs (determined by MIN(timestamp) per run_id) in ascending order until the count is at or below the limit
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: the number of distinct run_ids is at or below AF_AUDIT_MAX_RUNS after the step; the most recent runs are retained
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a retention run executes step 2

acceptance_criteria.action: delete hub_audit_events records older than AF_AUDIT_MAX_AGE_DAYS
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: hub_audit_events rows older than the configured max age are removed
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a retention run executes step 3

acceptance_criteria.action: delete completed agent_sessions (status in completed, failed, timeout, terminated) older than AF_SESSION_MAX_AGE_DAYS
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: terminal sessions older than the configured max age are removed; active sessions are never deleted by retention
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a retention run executes step 4

acceptance_criteria.action: delete token_usage rows whose session_id references a session that no longer exists in agent_sessions
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: orphaned token_usage rows are removed; rows linked to existing sessions are retained
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a retention run executes step 5

acceptance_criteria.action: delete agent_traces records older than AF_TRACE_MAX_AGE_DAYS
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: agent_traces rows older than the configured max age are removed
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a retention run executes step 6

acceptance_criteria.action: delete postmortems records older than AF_POSTMORTEM_MAX_AGE_DAYS
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: postmortems rows older than the configured max age are removed
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a retention run executes step 7

acceptance_criteria.action: query workspace slugs from SQLite in-memory, then delete DuckDB audit records whose workspace_slug is not in that set and whose ingestion timestamp exceeds AF_AUDIT_ORPHAN_RETENTION_DAYS
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: orphaned audit data older than the grace period is removed; data for existing workspaces is retained
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a retention run executes step 8

acceptance_criteria.action: update afhub_audit_table_rows gauge with COUNT(*) per audit table; recalibrate afhub_agent_sessions_active gauge via COUNT(*) WHERE status='active' GROUP BY workspace_slug
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Before applying query results, call GaugeVec.Reset() to clear all label combinations. Then set each (workspace_slug, status) pair from the query. This guarantees no stale label combinations persist across recalibration intervals, at the cost of a brief gap during reset. Gauge values reflect current row counts after the step completes.
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a retention run executes step 9

acceptance_criteria.action: set afhub_retention_last_run_timestamp_seconds to the current Unix timestamp and log rows deleted per table via slog
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: afhub_retention_last_run_timestamp_seconds reflects the completion time of the successful run
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a retention run completes all steps without context cancellation

acceptance_criteria.action: before deleting old closed sessions (step 4), force-close sessions WHERE status='active' AND started_at < NOW() - INTERVAL AF_SESSION_MAX_ACTIVE_AGE_DAYS DAYS, setting status='timeout' and ended_at=NOW()
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: active sessions older than AF_SESSION_MAX_ACTIVE_AGE_DAYS days are transitioned to status='timeout' with ended_at set to the current time; no active session older than the configured threshold remains in the agent_sessions table after this pre-step
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a retention run executes the pre-step before step 4

edge_cases.action: log the error via slog with the table name and error details, increment afhub_retention_errors_total with the appropriate step label, and continue executing the remaining steps
edge_cases.return_contract: subsequent steps execute; afhub_retention_last_run_timestamp_seconds is not updated if any step fails
edge_cases.error_condition: any of steps 1-9 returns a DuckDB error during a retention run

edge_cases.action: skip deletion and proceed to step 3
edge_cases.return_contract: no rows are deleted; the step completes without error
edge_cases.trigger: step 2 runs and the distinct run_id count is already at or below AF_AUDIT_MAX_RUNS

edge_cases.action: treat all DuckDB audit records as potentially orphaned and apply the grace period filter before deleting
edge_cases.return_contract: only records older than AF_AUDIT_ORPHAN_RETENTION_DAYS are deleted
edge_cases.trigger: step 8 runs and the SQLite workspace slug query returns an empty list

edge_cases.action: use AF_AUDIT_MAX_AGE_DAYS=90, AF_AUDIT_MAX_RUNS=50, AF_TRACE_MAX_AGE_DAYS=30, AF_SESSION_MAX_AGE_DAYS=90, AF_POSTMORTEM_MAX_AGE_DAYS=180, AF_AUDIT_ORPHAN_RETENTION_DAYS=30 when environment variables are not set
edge_cases.return_contract: retention runs with the documented default values
edge_cases.trigger: a retention run executes with default configuration values

user_story.goal: paginate through sessions and usage records using opaque cursors
user_story.benefit: so that I can retrieve large result sets without skipping or duplicating records

acceptance_criteria.action: encode pagination cursors as URL-safe base64 (RFC 4648 §5, no padding) tuples: (started_at, id) for GET /api/v1/sessions and (reported_at, id) for GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: cursors are opaque strings that clients must not construct or parse

acceptance_criteria.action: filter results using WHERE (started_at, id) < (cursor_started_at, cursor_id) for sessions or WHERE (reported_at, id) < (cursor_reported_at, cursor_id) for usage records
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns the next page of results in descending order without duplicates
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller provides a cursor with desc order

acceptance_criteria.action: filter results using WHERE (started_at, id) > (cursor_started_at, cursor_id) for sessions or WHERE (reported_at, id) > (cursor_reported_at, cursor_id) for usage records
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns the next page of results in ascending order without duplicates
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller provides a cursor with asc order

edge_cases.action: set next_cursor to null and has_more to false
edge_cases.return_contract: response contains next_cursor: null and has_more: false
edge_cases.trigger: the last page of results is returned

edge_cases.action: return 400 Bad Request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller provides a cursor that is not valid URL-safe base64 or does not decode to a valid (timestamp, id) tuple

correctness_properties.title: Session Open Idempotency
correctness_properties.invariant: the agent_sessions table contains exactly one row with that id regardless of how many times the request is submitted

correctness_properties.title: Session Close Idempotency on Terminal States
correctness_properties.for_any: session in any terminal status (completed, failed, timeout, or terminated)
correctness_properties.invariant: calling POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete returns 200 with the existing status and does not modify the session record

correctness_properties.title: Active Session Gauge Accuracy
correctness_properties.invariant: afhub_agent_sessions_active gauge for that workspace equals the COUNT(*) of agent_sessions rows with status=active for that workspace_slug, after any session open, close, or force-close operation

correctness_properties.title: Usage Totals Are Unbounded and Consistent
correctness_properties.for_any: session with any number of token_usage records
correctness_properties.invariant: the totals field in GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage always equals the SUM of all token_usage rows for that session regardless of pagination page or time range

correctness_properties.title: Keyset Pagination No Skip or Duplicate
correctness_properties.for_any: sequence of paginated requests to GET /api/v1/sessions or GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage
correctness_properties.invariant: the union of all pages equals the full result set with no duplicated or skipped records, even under concurrent inserts

correctness_properties.title: Force-Close Only Affects Active Sessions
correctness_properties.for_any: workspace with a mix of active and terminal sessions
correctness_properties.invariant: force-close sets status=terminated only on sessions with status=active; sessions in any terminal state are not modified

correctness_properties.title: Retention Last Run Timestamp Updated Only on Full Success
correctness_properties.for_any: retention run that fails any step
correctness_properties.invariant: afhub_retention_last_run_timestamp_seconds is not updated if any retention step fails; it is updated only after all 10 steps complete without error

correctness_properties.title: Ownership Enforcement on Session Mutations
correctness_properties.for_any: credential that is not the session owner and not an admin_token

correctness_properties.title: Cost Endpoint Time Range Validation
correctness_properties.for_any: since and until parameters where since >= until
correctness_properties.invariant: GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost returns 400 with error message 'since must be before until'

correctness_properties.title: Retention Worker Step Independence
correctness_properties.for_any: retention step that fails with a DuckDB error
correctness_properties.invariant: all subsequent steps still execute; the failure of one step does not prevent other steps from running

correctness_properties.title: Terminated Status Is Internal-Only
correctness_properties.invariant: the handler rejects the request with 400; terminated status can only be set by force-close logic

correctness_properties.title: Workspace Access Scoping for Non-Admin Callers
correctness_properties.for_any: non-admin caller accessing sessions or cost data for an inaccessible workspace
correctness_properties.invariant: the handler returns 403 Forbidden when an explicit workspace_slug filter or path parameter targets an inaccessible workspace

execution_paths.title: Agent Session Open to Close with Token Usage

steps.action: sends POST /api/v1/sessions with workspace_slug and optional metadata; authenticated via apikit.AuthInfo
validates workspace_slug is present; extracts credential_id and credential_type from apikit.AuthInfo; generates UUID if id not provided
inserts a new agent_sessions row with status=active into DuckDB; returns existing row if id already exists
increments afhub_agent_sessions_active gauge for the workspace; returns HTTP 201 (or 200 for duplicate) with session JSON
sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage with model and token counts
loads session record from Store; verifies caller is session owner or admin_token; checks session status is active
inserts a new token_usage row linked to the session in DuckDB
increments afhub_agent_tokens_total counter; returns HTTP 201 with token_usage record
sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete with status=completed and final token counts
loads session record; verifies ownership; updates session status to completed, sets ended_at and duration_ms in DuckDB
decrements afhub_agent_sessions_active gauge for the workspace; returns HTTP 200 with updated session record
sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/archive via the workspace API
updates workspace status to archived in SQLite
calls force-close logic for all active sessions in the workspace
updates all active agent_sessions rows for the workspace: sets status=terminated, ended_at=archive timestamp, error_message='workspace archived' in DuckDB
decrements afhub_agent_sessions_active gauge for each force-closed session

emits a hub.session.force_closed HubEvent for each force-closed session with ActorType='system', ActorID='', ResourceType='session', Action='terminate', and Metadata containing session_id and reason='workspace archived'
returns the archive response to the operator
calls StartRetentionWorker(ctx, store, sqliteDB) at hub startup
executes an immediate retention run before the first ticker fires

checks ctx.Err() before each step; executes steps 1-8 sequentially: deletes aged agent records, enforces run-count limit, deletes aged hub events, deletes aged sessions, deletes orphaned token_usage, deletes aged traces, deletes aged postmortems, deletes orphaned workspace audit data
executes each DELETE query against DuckDB; queries SQLite for workspace slugs for orphan detection (step 8)
executes step 9: updates afhub_audit_table_rows gauge with COUNT(*) per table; recalibrates afhub_agent_sessions_active gauge
executes step 10: sets afhub_retention_last_run_timestamp_seconds to current Unix timestamp; logs rows deleted per table via slog
waits for next tick (1 hour) or ctx.Done(), then repeats
sends GET /metrics to the hub's public port
routes the request to the promhttp handler mounted outside the API auth middleware group
collects all metrics from the custom Prometheus registry
returns HTTP 200 with Prometheus text exposition format containing all afhub_* metric values

execution_paths.title: End-to-End: Agent Session Lifecycle with Cost Query

steps.action: sends POST /api/v1/sessions with workspace_slug='my-workspace'; receives HTTP 201 with session id
creates agent_sessions row in DuckDB via Store; increments afhub_agent_sessions_active for 'my-workspace'
sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage three times with different models and token counts
inserts three token_usage rows in DuckDB; handler increments afhub_agent_tokens_total for each
sends POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete with status=completed
updates agent_sessions row to completed in DuckDB; decrements afhub_agent_sessions_active
sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/my-workspace/cost?group_by=model&since=...&until=...
verifies caller has access to 'my-workspace'; queries token_usage rows in DuckDB filtered by reported_at in [since, until)
aggregates token counts grouped by model; counts distinct session IDs with at least one token_usage record
returns HTTP 200 with totals and model-grouped breakdown including session count
sends GET /metrics; receives updated afhub_agent_tokens_total and afhub_agent_sessions_active values reflecting the completed session

error_handling.condition: POST /api/v1/sessions is called with a missing or empty workspace_slug
error_handling.behavior: handler calls apikit.WriteAPIError(c, 400, 'workspace_slug is required') and returns HTTP 400 with JSON body {error: 'workspace_slug is required', status: 400}
handler returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body indicating terminated is not a valid client-settable status

error_handling.condition: POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/complete or POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage is called by a non-owner non-admin credential
error_handling.behavior: handler returns HTTP 403 Forbidden after comparing credential_id from apikit.AuthInfo against the stored session record

error_handling.condition: POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage is called on a session with status not equal to active
error_handling.behavior: handler returns HTTP 409 Conflict with JSON body {error: 'session is not active'}

error_handling.condition: GET /api/v1/sessions is called with an explicit workspace_slug filter for a workspace the non-admin caller cannot access
GET /api/v1/sessions/:id is called for a session in a workspace the non-admin caller cannot access
GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost is called with since >= until
error_handling.behavior: handler returns HTTP 400 with JSON body {error: 'since must be before until'}

error_handling.condition: GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/cost is called by a non-admin caller for an inaccessible workspace
DuckDB force-close operation fails during workspace archive or delete
error_handling.behavior: the workspace handler logs a warning via slog and proceeds with the workspace lifecycle operation; sessions may remain active and will be treated as orphans by the retention worker

error_handling.condition: A retention step fails with a DuckDB error
error_handling.behavior: the retention worker logs the error via slog with table name and error details, increments afhub_retention_errors_total with the appropriate step label, and continues executing remaining steps; afhub_retention_last_run_timestamp_seconds is not updated

error_handling.condition: A pagination cursor cannot be decoded or parsed as a valid tuple
error_handling.behavior: handler returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body

error_handling.condition: SQLite workspace deletion fails after DuckDB sessions have been force-closed
error_handling.behavior: handler returns HTTP 500; sessions remain safely closed in DuckDB with terminated status

error_handling.condition: GET /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage is called for a session in an inaccessible workspace by a non-admin caller
error_handling.behavior: handler returns HTTP 403 Forbidden after loading the session record and checking workspace access

error_handling.condition: POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage is called with a missing or empty model field
error_handling.behavior: handler returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body

error_handling.condition: POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/usage is called with any of input_tokens, output_tokens, or cache_read_tokens set to a negative integer
error_handling.behavior: handler validates token counts before any DuckDB write and returns HTTP 422 with apikit.WriteAPIError message 'token counts must be non-negative'
